## THE PREREGISTRATION MOMENT

::: {.none}
1. Open the preregistration block in your report
2. Complete fields 1–5 – claim · data-in-hand · your one specification · DAG sentence · support/undermine rule
3. **Render**, or on the browser lab page copy the completed cell into your notes
4. Type **"declared"** in chat – then wait for the class
:::

::: {.fragment}
Nobody runs a model until everyone in the class has declared.
:::

::: notes
This is the moment that the day is named after, and we do it synchronously, because a thing that the whole class does at once sticks in a way that an instruction does not. Open Task 5. Fill in the five fields: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, your one specification across the fourteen axes, the one-sentence justification that your graph gives you, and the rule – written now, before any result – for what would support the claim and what would undermine it. Render the report; the rendered file with its timestamp is your record, like the frozen snapshot of a real registration. On the browser lab page, copy the completed cell into your notes. Then type "declared" in chat, and wait. [count them in aloud: "eight declared… twelve…"] Nobody runs anything until the whole class is in. And if you now want to declare the same specification you already explored before the break – that is allowed, and you should say so in the block. Declaring a specification whose result you have already seen is not preregistration.
:::

## Run it – then watch the chart {.smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Task 5** – run your declared specification, and only that one
- `report_result()` prints a one-click link with your numbers already in it – click, submit
- Your dot joins the **Multiverse** page as a *declared* result, beside the exploratory ones from before the break
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Compare the two waves. If the declared cloud falls systematically to one side of the exploratory cloud, it is worth discussing why.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Stuck? Chat "STUCK" · reload and rerun · second browser · follow my screen · last resort: the grid lookup on the menu page gives you your numbers by hand
:::

::: notes
Go. Run the specification you declared, just that one, and when the numbers are in front of you call report underscore result: it prints a link with your values already filled in, one click and you have submitted. Your dot joins the chart as a declared result, and it appears beside the exploratory dots that the class put up before the break. If the declared cloud falls systematically to one side of the exploratory cloud, that tells you something about what people chose to commit to once they had seen the alternatives, and it is worth a conversation. If anything misbehaves: type STUCK in chat and work down the ladder on the cheatsheet. And if your machine is truly finished for the day, the menu page shows you how to read the numbers for your specification straight off the published grid. Everybody gets a dot on the chart, no exceptions.
:::
